Q1.question: Project purpose and why it exists
Q1.value: The ADLC Discovery Tool is a structured, evidence-led engagement tool — a DataArt-led Solution Design engagement diagnosing SDLC bottlenecks and mapping a path to AI-first workflow adoption for the client. The harness tracks design work, engineering decisions, and skill patterns from discovery through publication.

Q2.question: Languages, frameworks, runtime, datastore, cloud; propose from config
Q2.value: TypeScript throughout. Web: VitePress 1.x on Vite. Auth: Node.js Lambda@Edge. Infrastructure: AWS CDK. Static origin: S3, served via CloudFront.

Q3.question: Named containers/layers; drives CONTAINER_LIST and specialist scope

Q4.question: Primary data flow and integrations
Q4.value: Browser → CloudFront (Lambda@Edge auth gate) → S3 (VitePress static build)

Q5.question: Tracker (Jira/Linear/GitHub Issues/none); ticket prefix, tracker URL, optional Confluence/board details
Q5.value: No external issue tracker. Internal ticket prefix: ADLC (e.g. ADLC-001). Story folders in docs/Stories/. No Jira/Confluence URLs.

Q6.question: Claude Code/Codex CLI/Cursor/Kiro/Windsurf/multiple; select installation paths and exactly one project instruction destination
Q6.value: Claude Code only. Codex projections (.agents/, .codex/, AGENTS.md) retired on 2026-09-15 — decided with the developer to drop cross-provider generation when adopting harness-bootstrap canonical as the sole source of truth (see run report for this launch).

Q7.question: Commit format, branch naming, build/check commands, guarded commands
Q7.value: Commit format: Conventional Commits (`<type>(<scope>): <what>`). Branch format: `<type>/short-description`. Package manager: yarn (never npm/npx). Guarded commands (never run directly, present as developer instructions): `cdk deploy`, `yarn nx run infra:provision`. `git push` runs after explicit per-action approval, never silently. Region must never be hardcoded in source or docs — deployment configuration only.

Q8.question: Confirmed NFR targets: availability, latency, residency, accessibility, cost, etc.
Q8.value: See docs/Target Architecture (HLD)/v1/Non-Functional Concerns/Requirements.md. Key: basic auth password protection on all routes (NFR-1), credentials from Secrets Manager not hardcoded (NFR-2), region never hardcoded (NFR-3), infra as code via CDK (NFR-4), VitePress build fails on dead links (NFR-5), giscus comments gated by GitHub repo permission (NFR-6). No cost ceiling; small team, ~10 internal users; fixed-duration engagement.

Q9.question: Team, pace, risks, other constraints
Q9.value: Small team, internal access only (~10 users); fixed-duration engagement scope; no cost ceiling defined.

Q10.question: Enabled Dev/Design/Skill/Architecture lifecycles; default all, Dev required
Q10.value: All four lifecycles enabled: Dev, Design, Skill, Architecture (all present under .claude/skills/)

Q10b.question: If Design: Project-scoped (default), Product-context-scoped, or Two-track; propose from detected shared docs
Q10b.value: Two-track — confirmed with developer 2026-08-16. /design supports both Product (docs/AI SDLC/, @discovery-owned engagement content) and Project (docs/Target Architecture (HLD)/, this repo's own architecture) tracks, resolved per session in Frame.

Q10c.question: If Product-context or Two-track: shared folder under project:docs/; propose detected name or Product Context
Q10c.value: PRODUCT_CONTEXT_DIR = AI SDLC — confirmed with developer 2026-08-16.

Q11.question: Azure/AWS/GCP/custom WAF with explicit pillars, or None; governs assessments and NFR output
Q11.value: AWS WAF (6 pillars: Reliability, Security, Cost Optimisation, Operational Excellence, Performance Efficiency, Sustainability) — matches installed war-design/SKILL.md pillar table.
